messages.text: Write a message telling my team the shop opens late on Monday.

Hi team, I hope you're all doing well! I wanted to let you know that the shop will be opening later than usual on Monday, at [time]. Please plan accordingly, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions. Thank you for your understanding!

slides.title: Give it a **hard limit.**
paras: Not "keep it short." A number: words, lines or bullets.

cards.title: No waffle
cards.text: [YOUR REQUEST]. Max [N] words. Lead with the key fact. No "I hope you're well", no filler at the end.

messages.text: Tell my team the shop opens at 11 on Monday, not 9 (stock delivery). Max 25 words. Lead with the key fact.
Heads-up: on Monday the shop opens at 11, not 9, because of a stock delivery. See you then!

caption:
How to make AI keep it short (and stop the waffle)

Ask for a simple team message and you get "I hope you're all doing well", "please plan accordingly" and a thank-you paragraph. All that for one fact: the shop opens late on Monday.

"Keep it short" doesn't really work. A number does:

"[YOUR REQUEST]. Max [N] words. Lead with the key fact. No "I hope you're well", no filler at the end."

With a 25-word limit, the same message became one line: Monday we open at 11, not 9, because of a stock delivery.

Other limits that work: "3 bullets, one line each" or "one sentence first, details after".

Bonus: already got a long one? Paste it back with "Cut this in half. Keep every fact."
